slides.say: a and b are prime numbers. Exactly two of the numbers fourteen, twenty-one and five are divisible by a. Exactly one of the numbers twenty-six, twenty-one and forty-two is divisible by b. What is a times b?

So a and b are primes, and the clues tell us which numbers they divide. Divisible by a prime means that prime is inside the number. So the first thing is to break every number into primes. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, breaking the numbers into primes, and then plugging in the answers.
[short pause] The first group. Fourteen is two times seven. Twenty-one is three times seven. And five is a prime.

Exactly two of them divide by a. So which prime shows up in exactly two of them? Two is only in fourteen. Three is only in twenty-one. Five is only in five. Seven is in fourteen and in twenty-one, exactly two. So a is seven.
The second group. Twenty-six is two times thirteen. Twenty-one is three times seven. Forty-two is six times seven, so two times three times seven.

Now exactly one of them divides by b. Two is in twenty-six and forty-two, that's two numbers. Three is in twenty-one and forty-two, two again. Seven is in twenty-one and forty-two, two again. Thirteen is only in twenty-six. So b is thirteen.

So a times b is seven times thirteen. Seven times ten is seventy, and seven times three is twenty-one, together ninety-one. Choice number three is our answer. And remember ninety-one, the fake prime from the start of the topic.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Each choice is a product of two primes. So I split it, and check which one could be a, and the other one b.

Choice number one, thirty-nine, is three times thirteen. Could a be three? Only twenty-one divides by three, that's one number, not two. Could a be thirteen? None of fourteen, twenty-one and five divides by thirteen. Out.
Choice number two, twenty-six, is two times thirteen. Is a two? Only fourteen divides by two. Is a thirteen? None. Out.

Choice number three, ninety-one, is seven times thirteen. a is seven, and fourteen and twenty-one divide by seven, exactly two. Then b is thirteen, and only twenty-six divides by thirteen, exactly one. It fits.

In the exam you'd circle it and move on. Here, let's check the last one too. Twenty-one is three times seven. a can't be three, because only one number divides by three. So a is seven, and b is three. But three divides twenty-one and forty-two, that's two numbers, not one. Out. So choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
